system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
## Buyer-side review — Project Kestrel

| Issue | Seller’s position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% of price / AUD 4.8m**. | At least **40–50% of price (AUD 9.6m–12m)**, with separate higher caps for tax, title, fundamental warranties and specific indemnities. | **Reject 20%; propose 50%.** A AUD 4.8m cap is inadequate for a AUD 24m acquisition, particularly given unresolved diligence matters. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 deductible basket, with only excess recoverable. | No de minimis for related claims; otherwise **AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 tipping basket**, excluding tax, fundamental and indemnity claims. | **Counter with lower thresholds and a tipping basket.** Seller’s formulation leaves Buyer bearing the first AUD 250,000 even after a material pattern of breaches emerges. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General Warranty Claims expire **18 months after Completion**; Seller seeks to apply limitations to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24–36 months** for general warranties, with separate periods for tax, title, fraud and specific indemnities. | **Reject 18 months and the blanket formulation; propose 24 months minimum.** Many accounting, customer and operational issues will only emerge through multiple reporting cycles. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the same **20% cap and 18-month limit** as general warranties. | Capacity, authority, ownership and title warranties capped at **100% of purchase price**, with at least the applicable statutory limitation period; no de minimis or basket. | **Reject general-warranty treatment.** Buyer must have full recourse if Seller cannot validly sell, or does not own, all acquired shares. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to **all Claims of any nature**; no express fraud carve-out. | Express carve-out for **fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment and deliberate breach**, overriding all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance provisions. | **Insist on an overriding fraud carve-out.** Seller must not benefit from contractual protections where information has been dishonestly or deliberately withheld. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | Entire indexed data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records are generally disclosed. | Only matters **fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify their nature, scope and reasonably foreseeable effect**, preferably by specific disclosure against identified warranties; frozen disclosure bundle. | **Reject blanket data-room and public-record disclosure.** Buyer should not bear the risk of locating or inferring exceptions from a mass of documents. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by Buyer or advisers, including anything **discoverable** from the data room or public records. | No knowledge qualifier, or at most **actual knowledge of a short list of named Buyer deal-team individuals**, without enquiry, constructive knowledge or adviser attribution; disclosure rules remain controlling. | **Delete constructive and imputed knowledge.** A discoverability standard converts diligence into a broad waiver of negotiated warranty protection. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller will use reasonable endeavours; condition treated as satisfied upon delivery of written consent, despite missing evidence that clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied. | A true **condition precedent** requiring final written consent, satisfaction of all associated conditions, and no adverse amendment, fee or waiver, all in form acceptable to Buyer. | **Do not permit deemed satisfaction or waiver without Buyer consent.** Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue and its continuity is fundamental to valuation. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m remains outstanding; release to be provided **following Completion**. | At or before Completion: binding payout letter, repayment through funds flow, termination of facility, and release of all guarantees, security interests and PPSR registrations. | **Make simultaneous discharge a Completion deliverable.** Buyer must not acquire the Company subject to Seller-era debt or security in a debt-free/cash-free deal. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are Seller’s matter and omitted from funds flow; on-costs are unquantified. | Treat bonuses and all payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs as **Seller transaction expenses/debt-like items**, deducted from price or paid and fully provided for at Completion. | **Add the grossed-up amount to funds flow and adjustment mechanics.** Completion-triggered bonuses arise from the sale and should not reduce post-Completion value. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific unpaid **AUD 180,000 SOW3 fee**. | Payment before Completion, receipt and confirmatory IP assignment; otherwise a standalone indemnity covering all losses from non-payment, defective ownership or transfer, third-party claims and remediation relating to SOW3 materials. | **Broaden the indemnity and require evidence of title.** Paying the invoice alone may not cure or compensate for an existing chain-of-title defect. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Characterised as preliminary and not expected to be material; access, scope, notification and loss remain unconfirmed. | Completion investigation and containment plan, preservation of evidence, required notifications, continuing cooperation, and a specific indemnity for all pre-Completion incident-related losses, remediation, claims and regulatory action. | **Do not accept disclosure as the sole treatment.** The incident affects about 1,240 records and presently has unquantified regulatory, contractual and reputational exposure. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three AUD 110,000 renewals are said to be ordinary-course operating costs. | Evidence of terms, timing, termination rights, accrual and necessity; no renewal or commitment without Buyer consent, and price adjustment for pre-Completion or non-ordinary-course liabilities. | **Require substantiation and appropriate price treatment.** The aggregate AUD 330,000 commitment cannot be assumed ordinary-course merely because Seller labels it so. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Seller seeks to apply limitations to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise. | Express, mutually exclusive regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities, covenants, debt/leakage and fraud, with no accidental cross-application of limitations. | **Rewrite the limitations clause by claim category.** A blanket “all Claims” formulation could nullify the negotiated protection for known high-risk matters. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on DD-012 share register as evidence that Seller holds 100% of the shares. | Original or replacement share certificates, constitution and issue/transfer records, ASIC and PPSR searches, confirmation of legal and beneficial ownership, no options or third-party rights, releases and executed transfers. | **Make complete title evidence a Completion requirement.** A company-maintained register alone does not establish unencumbered legal and beneficial title. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties are treated as settled under the general 20%/18-month regime. | Separate tax covenant/indemnity for pre-Completion tax, generally capped at 100% and surviving through the relevant statutory review period plus a buffer; robust IP ownership, validity, infringement, open-source and employee/contractor assignment warranties with an appropriate higher cap and longer survival. | **Keep tax and IP outside the general regime.** Both can create substantial latent liabilities that are unlikely to crystallise within 18 months or fit within a 20% cap. |

### Overall position

The Seller package should not be accepted as a combined risk allocation. In particular, Buyer should make **Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, title evidence and satisfactory Ironquay IP treatment hard Completion requirements**, while placing the bonuses, privacy incident and other identified liabilities into express price-adjustment or specific-indemnity regimes.
=== END ADVICE ===
